Joanna: Nate, after finishing my screenplay I got a rejection letter from a major company. It really bummed me out.
Nate: Sorry to hear that, Joanna. Rejection stinks, but it doesn't mean you're not talented. Don't give up on your dreams!
Joanna: Thanks, Nate. It can feel like a step back sometimes. But I appreciate your kind words and encouragement.
Nate: Sure, just make sure you keep going and believing in yourself. Did something happen with the company?
Joanna: They just sent me a generic rejection letter without much feedback. It's disheartening not knowing why it didn't work out.
Nate: Ugh, that's so frustrating. But don't get discouraged, just keep going.
Joanna: Yeah, you're right. I won't let this bring me down. Thanks for your support. What have you been up to lately?
Nate: I've been doing great - I just won another regional video game tournament last week! It was so cool, plus I met some new people. Connecting with fellow gamers is always awesome.
Joanna: Way to go, Nate! Congratulations on your victory in the tournament! It must feel great to be recognized for your gaming skills.
Nate: Thanks, Joanna! Winning was a huge confidence boost and shows my hard work paid off. I'm really happy with my progress.
Joanna: I am as well! It's great to hear from you about your tournaments throughout the years!
Nate: Thanks! I has been a while since my first tournament hasn't it? I appreciate your support!
Joanna: Anytime Nate! I'm here for you every step of the way.
Nate: I talked to some of the guys at the tournament afterwards, and they said they wanted to hang out later!
Joanna: Sounds like fun! It's good to have friends that share your interests!
Nate: For sure! They asked for some tips in how to improve their game, so I said I could help.
Joanna: Good on you for helping strangers out! Stepping outside your comfort zone is always great.
Nate: Thanks, I just like helping people. Do you have any plans for the weekend?
Joanna: Yep, I'm hiking with some buddies this weekend. We're checking out a new trail with a rad waterfall. Can't wait! Do you have any fun plans?
Nate: Sounds great! Have fun with that. I'm organizing a gaming party two weekends later - it'll be hectic but fun!
Joanna: Oh? Are you going to invite your tournament friends?
Nate: Definitely! And some old friends and teamates from other tournaments.
Joanna: Sounds like fun, Nate! I wish you the best on your party. Have a blast!
Nate: Thanks Joanna! I'm sure it'll be a blast. I'm even getting everyone custom controller decorations just for coming!
Joanna: Wow, I bet they'll love that! What a sweet idea.
Nate: I know right? Have a great hike. Take lots of pics! See ya later!
Joanna: Thanks Nate! See you later!

Joanna: Hey Nate, long time no talk! I've been busy with writing projects and really going all out with it. It's been the best thing ever - a mix of highs and lows - and my journal's pretty much my rock. Writing's such a huge part of me now.

Nate: Nice work, Joanna! That must feel sureal. Keep it up - you're changing lives!

Joanna: Yum, Nate! I love it when you make coconut milk icecream, it's so good!
Nate: I've been really into making this lately - it's creamy, rich, dairy-free and a new recipe! Wanna try it? I can share the recipe with you if you'd like!
Joanna: I'd love to try it! Thanks for sharing your love for dairy-free desserts. I really appreciate it!
Nate: No problem, Joanna! Always happy to share them with you. Sending you the recipe now!
Joanna: Thanks, Nate! Can't wait to surprise my family with something delicious!
Nate: No problem, Joanna! Wish them luck! Let me know how it goes. Have a blast baking!
Joanna: Thanks, Nate. I'll keep you posted. Have a great day.
Nate: You too!

If the exact month/day is unknown, record at least the start year, phrasing it as 'started in YYYY' or 'since YYYY'.

selected.name: Extract Explicit Goals and Intended Impact
selected.description: Use when a message states a hope, goal, dream, or intended impact for an activity or interest.
content: During extraction, if a message explicitly states a user's goal, hope, aspiration, or intended impact for an activity (e.g., share stories, make a difference, reach others), capture it as a separate facet in the memory content; do not replace it with only current emotional benefits like escape, expression, or healing.
When enriching an existing memory, preserve previously stored facets and ADD the newly stated goal or impact rather than overwriting the memory with a narrower paraphrase.
Stop after capturing the explicit goal and its immediate context; do not enumerate every possible future hope or infer unstated ambitions.
selected.rerank_reason: Joanna explicitly states her goal of making a difference through writing, which is a clear indication of an intended impact.

nearby_not_selected.name: Extract Comfort and Joy Sources
nearby_not_selected.description: Use when a message states that something cheers the user up, brings joy, or provides comfort.
content: During extraction, if the user mentions a pet, hobby, person, item, or activity that provides cheer, comfort, or emotional support, create a separate durable memory (preference, relationship, or state) capturing that source, even when the message also contains stress or negative events.
Do not merge the supportive source only into a negative-event candidate; it should be its own candidate so it survives later SKIP/MERGE decisions.
Extract only sources explicitly stated as supportive; do not infer unmentioned ones.

nearby_not_selected.name: Extract Statements of Personal Significance
nearby_not_selected.description: Use when a user says an object, photo, or item reminds them of someone or something, or has personal meaning.
content: During extraction, when a user describes an object, photo, or item as reminding them of someone or something ('reminds me of', 'makes me think of', 'means ... to me'), create a candidate state memory capturing the connection.
Record who is reminded (the speaker), the object, and what it reminds them of (person, feeling, or value) in the speaker's own words.
Treat such statements as durable personal facts even though they are phrased as effects or feelings, not as direct assertions; extract at most one memory per statement.

nearby_not_selected.name: Extract Concrete Activity from Follow-Up Clarification
nearby_not_selected.description: Use when a message describes an activity vaguely and the next message names the concrete result.
content: During extraction, treat any message reporting the speaker performing an activity as a candidate source, even when the object is only a photo or pronoun.
If the following message from another participant identifies the concrete object or result, extract an event memory capturing who did what, using both messages as evidence.
Do not skip follow-up messages that clarify or name an earlier activity.

nearby_not_selected.name: Capture Brief Project Mentions with Full Attributes
nearby_not_selected.description: Use when a speaker mentions a project they completed, are working on, or plan to build, even briefly.
content: Create an event candidate for any explicit statement of a completed, ongoing, or planned project, even in small talk.
When several messages describe the same project, consolidate them into one candidate and include every explicit attribute stated.
Stop once the speaker has finished describing the project in that session.

nearby_not_selected.name: Extract Shared Bonding-Activity Memories
nearby_not_selected.description: When a user reflectively describes a past shared activity with a specific person and frames it as bonding, making memories, or quality time.
content: During extraction, treat first-person statements about a past shared activity with a named person that explicitly mention bonding, making memories, closeness, or quality time as a durable event or relationship memory candidate.
Capture the activity, the companion, and the relational framing.
Do not require explicit fact-like phrasing; reflective storytelling is sufficient evidence.
Create at most one candidate per distinct activity-and-companion pair, and skip statements that name no specific person or activity.
